Article Title: ‘Dissatisfied? You're not alone’: FIR filed over posters in Delhi Metro questioning govt
Article Text:
QR code posters questioning the government found inside a Delhi Metro train; FIR registered

NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons after two posters questioning the government's performance were found pasted inside a train on the Delhi Metro's Airport Express Line, news agency PTI reported citing police sources.The posters, printed in black and white on A4-sized sheets, featured phrases such as "Voting Protest", "You Can Change Your Own Life", "Spectrum of Engagement", "Community Building Reform" and "Dissatisfied? You Are Not Alone".They also listed nine claims about changes in the country in recent years and carried a QR code inviting people to join an online group, the sources said.According to the FIR, the incident came to light on October 20 when Tarun Chaudhary, a Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) train operator deployed on the Airport Express Line, spotted the posters during an inspection.Chaudhary had operated a train from New Delhi station to Yashobhoomi, leaving at around 6.50pm and arriving at approximately 7.15pm. While checking the train from inside the cabin, he noticed the two posters pasted on a seat.He removed the material and alerted his senior officers and the Operations Control Centre. He was subsequently instructed to hand the posters over to the station controller at Dwarka Sector 21, who informed the police.The posters were seized by police on Friday, and the special cell has also joined the investigation.
Article Summary: Two posters questioning the government's performance were found inside a train on the Delhi Metro's Airport Express Line. An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons. The posters featured phrases such as "Voting Protest" and "Dissatisfied? You Are Not Alone"

NEW DELHI: Kerala governor Om Prakash Mathur's reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only has sparked a political controversy, with Congress leader K C Venugopal accusing him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda.Mathur, the former Sikkim governor, directed that non-vegetarian food should not be prepared or served in the Lok Bhavan kitchen. The reports surfaced on Thursday, a day before he assumed office, news agency PTI reported.Reacting to the reports shortly after Mathur was sworn in as the 29th governor of Keralam, AICC general secretary Venugopal alleged that the decision went beyond the governor's personal food preferences and infringed on individual freedom.Keralam has a diverse food culture and abundant fish resources as a coastal state, Venugopal said, adding that people had the freedom to choose between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food."Any attempt to restrict the food habits Keralites are accustomed to or dictate what they should eat from now on cannot be accepted," he said as quoted by PTI.Venugopal argued that restrictions that "intrude" into people's food choices and seek to erase Keralam's traditional way of life violate fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.He alleged that the governor was using his authority to "curtail" individual freedom instead of protecting people's right to decide what to eat and how to live."This is a continuation of the unconstitutional interests of the Sangh Parivar. This is the first step towards implementing the saffron agenda of the Sangh Parivar in Keralam," the Alappuzha MP alleged.While acknowledging Mathur's right to follow a vegetarian diet, Venugopal said the governor should not impose his personal preferences on the Lok Bhavan kitchen, whose employees include Keralites. He urged Mathur to withdraw any decision restricting food choices.Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian and had directed that non-vegetarian food not be prepared in the kitchen where his meals were cooked.They clarified that the kitchen's food was served only to the governor and a few members of his personal staff. Other employees either brought food from home or ate outside, and no restrictions had been imposed on their food choices, the sources said as cited by PTI.They added that fish and meat dishes had been prepared in the Lok Bhavan kitchen during the tenure of some previous governors.
Article Summary: Kerala Governor Om Prakash Mathur’s reported decision to make the Lok Bhavan kitchen vegetarian-only sparks a row. Congress leader K C Venugopal accuses him of pushing the Sangh Parivar's agenda. Sources in the governor's office said Mathur was a strict vegetarian.

Article Title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border management remains in focus
Article Text:
File photo: ITBP personnel

Rajnath Singh, Kiren Rijiju salute ITBP personnel

Indian Army extends wishes on ITBP's 65th Raising Day

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju extended greetings to personnel of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) on the force's Raising Day on Saturday, praising their courage, sacrifices and service in protecting India's borders.The Indian Army also conveyed its wishes to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of the force's 65th Raising Day.In a post on X, Prime Minister Modi praised the force's personnel, known as Himveers, for their valour and determination in facing challenges.“On their Raising Day, greetings to all personnel of the ITBP. The ITBP Himveers have distinguished themselves through their exceptional valour. They have always risen to every challenge with remarkable determination. Their selfless service and sacrifices are a source of immense inspiration to the nation,” PM Modi wrote.Union home minister Amit Shah also extended Raising Day greetings to ITBP personnel, praising their courage in safeguarding the country's security and remembering those who laid down their lives in service to the nation.“The roar of their valour echoes through the snow-clad mountains, reducing every threat to our nation's security to rubble.Their tenacity in withstanding the harshest climates symbolizes India's steely resolve for security. Salutations to the martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation,” Shah wrote on X.Defence minister Rajnath Singh extended his greetings to ITBP personnel and their families, highlighting their contribution to border security and internal security operations.“On ITBP Raising Day, I extend my warm greetings to all ITBP personnel and their families. The Himveers of ITBP have played a vital role in safeguarding India’s borders in the harshest climatic conditions. They have also made significant contributions to internal security operations, including efforts to combat Left Wing Extremism,” Singh said.He added that their courage, professionalism and commitment to duty reflected the finest traditions of service to the nation.Kiren Rijiju also greeted the Himveers, invoking the force's motto, “शौर्य-दृढ़ता-कर्मनिष्ठा” (valour, steadfastness and devotion to duty).“On the occasion of ITBP Raising Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to the Himveers of @ITBP_official. Your vital resilience in protecting our borders in extreme conditions is an inspiration. Salute to your spirit of sacrifices & patriotism,” Rijiju wrote on X.The Indian Army also conveyed its greetings to the force. In a post on X, it said General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of Army Staff, and all ranks of the Army extended their “warm greetings and best wishes” to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of its 65th Raising Day.The ITBP is responsible for guarding India's borders with China in challenging high-altitude and climatic conditions.The greetings come amid continuing attention to the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday that the situation along the India-China border gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns.“Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC),” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.Jaiswal also said the two countries had agreed to discuss ways to improve their understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to strengthen border management. He stressed that maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur had recently spoken about continuing confrontations with Chinese troops at several locations along the border in Arunachal Pradesh.He also said the force had raised drone platoons in all its border units and developed a new 'Strike' course to better handle battles similar to the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju extended greetings to personnel of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police. The Indian Army also conveyed its wishes to ITBP personnel, veterans and their families on the occasion of the force's Raising Day.

Article Title: China’s patrolling deviations disturb border: MEA on ITBP DG's LAC face-offs remark
Article Text:
ITBP chief flags ‘ongoing’ China faceoff along Arunachal border.

The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off

Stronger drones must to counter PLA: ITBP

Cong slams govt over face-offs

New Delhi: Following confirmation by ITBP of the continuing India-China military stand-off on the Arunachal Pradesh border, India once again cautioned China that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral ties, echoing PM Narendra Modi’s message to Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting last month.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time.“As we have noted in the past, the situation in India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, adding that the two sides had also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control in appropriate areas for better border management.The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control.ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur had on Thursday publicly said that Indian and Chinese troops had lately been locked in face-offs at select points along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, which “are still continuing”. He, however, added that the ‘Shaurya’ commandos of his force, deployed along the LAC, had done an “excellent job” in dealing with the face-offs.The ITBP chief said India was focusing on building its drone and anti-drone capabilities as “conventional” military resources and infrastructure were not enough to take on the People’s Liberation Army which had undergone a massive capacity upgrade and modernisation, making China a “very strong adversary”.“Drones can pose a challenge as well as present an advantage,” Kapur said, citing the example of Ukraine and Iran which, despite being small nations and with much smaller or no conventional armed forces, had taken on superpowers like Russia and the US respectively.DG Shatrujeet Kapur said ITBP had included drone platoons for all its border units, with 70% of the Rs 400 crore allocated by MHA for modernisation of the force earmarked for upgrading drone warfare capabilities. The force is raising more ‘Shaurya’ commando platoons trained in mountain warfare, new-generation weapons and unarmed combat.Kapur said ITBP must redefine itself as a high-altitude fighting force, distinct from the Army or any other central paramilitary force.Reports of border friction coincide with the ongoing efforts to normalise Sino-India ties that have seen considerable progress since Modi’s meeting with Xi in Russia’s Kazan in 2024.In the meeting last month, Modi underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. The two leaders also expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question.Citing ITBP DG Shatrujeet Kapur’s remarks about continuing skirmishes with China, Congress Friday asked PM Modi whether the pre-May 2020 status quo ante had been restored in Ladakh and if India could patrol up to border points such as Shera-5 in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera said the govt should send an all-party delegation, including the opposition, to Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh to establish whether China had encroached on Indian territory.“PM gave China a clean chit in 2020. In 2026, the country deserves a clean account of what is happening on its borders. Enough of clean chits to China — it is time for govt to come clean before India.”Khera termed DG Shatrujeet Kapur’s remarks serious and claimed they showed that China’s belligerence continued despite the govt “kowtowing” to Beijing. He cited continuing skirmishes, reports of encroachment, including by BJP netas, and a trade deficit with China that had ballooned to $113 billion.Congress questioned outcomes of repeated meetings between Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping, asking why incursions and attempts to alter the LAC continued.
Article Summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off. India once again cautioned China that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral ties. The two sides had also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the Line of Actual Control.

Delhi HC rejects AISA chief Neha Bora’s plea against police ‘peace’ bond notice

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court rejected a plea filed by All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora challenging a police notice directing her to execute a bond for “keeping peace” before a Special Executive Magistrate."I am rejecting the writ petition at this juncture," Justice Subramonium Prasad said while pronouncing the judgment.The judge, however, issued directions to the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) to provide the student leader with all relevant material related to the proceedings.Bora had moved the high court on Monday, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a “colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution”.During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens do not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice which alleged that she had hoisted the flag without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety “for keeping peace for a period of enquiry.”Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings based on alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place on the same day.“The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner’s call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House,” Bora’s petition said.
Article Summary: The Delhi high court rejected a plea filed by All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora. Bora had challenged a police notice directing her to execute a bond for “keeping peace” before a Special Executive Magistrate. The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19.

Article Title: Siddaramaiah cries blackmail over ‘fake sting’ video, alleges conspiracy
Article Text:
Yathindra alleges Congress links to sting operation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah on Friday said he had lodged a police complaint over an alleged “fake sting operation” video targeting him, alleging that it was an attempt to blackmail him after he lost power.Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, the senior Congress leader said he wanted the truth to come out and those behind the video to be identified. He also said he had obtained an injunction from a civil court to prevent the video from being given further publicity.“This is a false case. This case was done with the intention to blackmail me. Therefore, I myself have filed a complaint so that the truth comes out. The people should know the truth and also who is behind this,” Siddaramaiah said.He alleged that the video was fabricated and said he had never faced such an incident during his earlier tenures in office.“I was chief minister for 8 years, at that time no incident of blackmailing me happened. Now I have no power,” he said.Siddaramaiah named Kripa Alva, a woman from Dakshina Kannada, and Rakesh Shetty as people who appeared in the video. He claimed that Shetty had admitted to carrying out the operation.“Rakesh Shetty himself has admitted that they did it. There is no truth in this video,” he said.Siddaramaiah said the video first came to his notice on September 26 and denied being worried about the allegations.“After I have not done any wrong, there is no question of me being upset. No matter who sets out to defame me, I know what the truth is. There is no question of me being upset or afraid. This case is 100% created,” he said.Recalling his political career, he said he first became a minister in 1984 and had faced no such incident even when he was chief minister.“Now when I have no power, such a conspiracy is being hatched. It is true that their intention will not succeed,” he asserted.Meanwhile, Karnataka minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah alleged that people from within the Congress were behind the purported sting operation, which he claimed was intended to damage his father's image and blackmail him.Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, Yathindra said the video appeared to show the involvement of a woman from the Congress who wanted a party ticket from Puttur, along with the head of a media organisation.“The whole thing was done to damage my father, tarnish his image, destroy his legacy and blackmail him,” Yathindra said.The minister, who holds the Urban Development portfolio, said the woman's alleged involvement appeared to be linked to her political ambitions.“There is a woman from our party who is involved. As she herself says in the video, she wanted a party ticket from Puttur. Prima facie, it appears that the sting operation was conducted for that purpose,” he said.However, Yathindra cautioned against holding the entire Congress responsible for the alleged actions of an individual party worker.“Just because a party worker has done something like this, it does not mean that our entire party is against us,” he said.
Article Summary: Former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah says he has lodged a police complaint over an alleged “fake sting operation” video targeting him. He alleges that the video was an attempt to blackmail him after he lost power. Karnataka minister Yathindra alleges that people from within the Congress were behind the purported sting operation, which he claimed was intended to damage his father's image.

Article Title: 'Won't tolerate vote theft': Anti-SIR protesters try to march to EC HQ, many detained

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police detained several protesters on Friday as a march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls headed towards the Election Commission (EC) headquarters in central Delhi. Authorities imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), banning mass gatherings, sources said.The demonstration was called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, a people's collective, and drew students, youth, farmers and activists carrying the national flag and banners of the group.The Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) and the Students' Federation of India (SFI) also extended their support, with activists from Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh joining the march.Amid slogans such as “Gyanesh Kumar, resign”, “Halt SIR” and “Won’t tolerate vote theft”, the protesters were joined by senior CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and members of the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA) and the All India Democratic Students' Organisation (AIDSO), among others.The march began near Gole Dak Khana, at the intersection of Kalibari Marg and Bhai Vir Singh Marg, and proceeded towards the ECI headquarters.When police stopped the protesters, they sat down and held a 'People's Parliament', as announced by the organisers.“The protest has begun! We won't let go our right to vote and the right to protest for it! Our's is a democratic country and we will ensure that spirit remains alive!” the All India Students' Association (AISA) said in a post on X.“This is not about reclaiming Jantar Mantar; this is about saving democracy and the country,” a protester said, as cited by PTI.Another protester said that since Jantar Mantar had been denotified as a protest site, every street in the country would become a Jantar Mantar, pointing to several organisations announcing demonstrations across India.People Against SIR has launched a website providing information about demonstrations being held in different cities. According to the collective, protests have been planned in 88 cities across 18 states, involving 145 organisations.The collective has listed demonstrations scheduled for Friday, with programmes extending until November 1 as part of its campaign against the SIR exercise. Organisers have appealed to farmers, workers, youth, women and people from different sections of society to participate while carrying the national flag.The organisers said the Delhi march would remain peaceful and conclude with the adoption of resolutions and the singing of the national anthem. The SFI has also called for solidarity protests in central Delhi and at district headquarters on Friday.Security was tightened in central Delhi, with Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed in large numbers.Traffic diversions were enforced in parts of central Delhi from 1 pm and were scheduled to remain in place until 5 pm. Congestion was expected around Bangla Sahib Gurudwara, Connaught Place, Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar.The Delhi Traffic Police advised commuters to avoid unnecessary travel along the affected stretches, plan their journeys and follow instructions issued by traffic personnel.The protest comes amid concerns raised by opposition parties and various organisations over the SIR exercise and the alleged deletion of voters from electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Demonstrators march towards Election Commission headquarters in central Delhi. Demonstration is part of campaign against Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Protests planned across 88 cities across 18 states, involving 145 organisations. Police impose prohibitory orders under Section 163 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

NEW DELHI: Speculation over a possible reunion between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) gathered pace on Friday after SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal said his party was open to an alliance with parties that agree with its ideology and programmes, a day after Union home minister Amit Shah predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027.Badal, however, ruled out any understanding with the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling them the “two biggest enemies of Punjab”."During the SAD-BJP rule, peace prevailed in Punjab, and the state witnessed development, be it in infrastructure, industry, or the state becoming power surplus," Badal told reporters on Friday, according to PTI."Whether we form the government or not, we will continue to fight for the people of Punjab. In our view, the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party are the two biggest enemies of Punjab, and we can never have understanding with these parties. There are many other parties besides these and those who agree with the Akali Dal's ideology and programmes; we are open (for a tie-up)," he said.The remarks came a day after Union minister Amit Shah said Punjab's people had decided that an NDA government would come to power in the state in the 2027 assembly elections.He also predicted that the ruling AAP would be wiped out in the polls.Shah's statement reignited speculation about the BJP and SAD joining hands again, although Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon denied that any alliance decision had been taken."We have nothing on an alliance as of now. We are prepared for all 117 seats and will contest on all of them," Dhillon told TOI, adding that the BJP referred to its government at the Centre as an NDA government and would do the same in Punjab.A senior Punjab BJP functionary, however, said the political signal was clear despite Shah not naming the Akali Dal. The functionary also felt the two parties should have announced an alliance earlier, given the limited time before the elections. Any formal announcement would have to come from BJP national president Nitin Nabin, the functionary said.The SAD and BJP were long-time allies in Punjab before the regional party ended their 24-year-old alliance in September 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws. SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Sukhbir Singh Badal's wife, had also served as a Cabinet minister in the Narendra Modi government before the split.The former allies contested elections together for years, but their political fortunes were limited in the 2022 Punjab assembly polls. The BJP won two seats, while the SAD secured three in the 117-member Assembly.In recent months, several Punjab BJP leaders had maintained that the party was preparing to contest all 117 assembly seats independently. Dhillon reiterated that position on Friday, even as Shah's remarks and Badal's openness to an alliance renewed questions about the parties' electoral plans.Badal made the comments after leading an SAD delegation to meet Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday. The delegation submitted a memorandum over the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and demanded, among other measures, the dismissal of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.Badal accused the AAP government of mishandling Punjab's affairs and said the state's law and order situation had deteriorated. He also blamed the Congress and AAP governments for what he described as the worsening situation in the state.With the 2027 assembly elections approaching, the public statements have revived the possibility of a realignment between the former allies. However, neither party has announced a formal agreement, and the BJP's Punjab leadership continues to maintain that it is preparing to contest all 117 seats.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of remaining silent on reported face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh. The party also alleged that the government had made ‘concessions’ to Beijing and failed to adequately address concerns over border security.In a post on X, the opposition party criticised PM over his interactions with Chinese president Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit, saying the prime minister was seen joking with Xi even as Indian troops reportedly faced tensions along the border."Instead of showing China the "red eye," Narendra Modi was seen joking around with Chinese President Xi Jinping—at the BRICS summit", it wrote.The Congress also alleged that reports of clashes with Chinese soldiers had been suppressed since July.The party's handle shared the video of the ITBP chief and wrote, “Modi has abandoned our soldiers every time, betrayed the country, and washed his hands of responsibility. Sometimes giving China a clean chit, sometimes abandoning control of patrolling points and the country's land. He called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a “weak prime minister” and accused him of causing immense damage to the country.The criticism follows remarks by Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, who said on Thursday that the force’s newly raised Shaurya commando unit had demonstrated its capabilities during ongoing face-offs with China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh.Kapoor said the specialised commandos would be deployed across every border battalion as the ITBP strengthens its combat readiness along the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control (LAC). The force is also expanding its modernisation drive, with greater emphasis on specialised training and emerging warfare technologies.Meanwhile, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh separately cited media reports about the recent face-offs, questioning the Centre’s silence on the developments. He criticised the government’s Make in India initiative, writing that it had effectively become “Import from China”, and described the widening trade gap as a threat to economic security.The Congress also invoked Modi’s June 19, 2020, remarks following the Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian soldiers were killed. Ramesh quoted the prime minister as saying that no one had entered Indian territory and that no Indian post was under another country’s control.
Article Summary: The Congress accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of remaining silent on reported face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh. NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday criticised the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House in New Delhi, saying the move had damaged India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy and raised serious concerns over freedom of expression.In a post on X, Tharoor described the incident as a "disgrace at so many levels", arguing that photographs documenting protest demonstrations depicted events and did not necessarily convey political positions."This is a disgrace at so many levels," Thiruvananthapuram MP said, listing his objections to the decision to remove the photographs from the exhibition, "No Idea Is Final".He said the images documented events that had already received widespread public and media attention, questioning why photographs of demonstrations should be considered political content simply because they depicted protests."The images are of events that have already been burned into the public consciousness, and many of the photos would have echoed similar images that the public has already seen in the media and online," Tharoor said, adding that "While Bikaner House is free to have a policy against political stands, photographs of a protest demonstration are a depiction of an event and not political in themselves; they would almost certainly have passed muster had the matter been brought to a court as an issue of freedom of expression.He further alleged that the decision had hurt India's international image."And worst of all, this censorship has driven one more nail into the coffin of India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy," the Congress MP said.Tharoor also pointed out that the controversy had brought significant attention to Raihan Vadra's photographic work, potentially exposing it to a much wider audience than the exhibition would otherwise have reached."Anyway, the publicity this episode has received will have reached a far larger audience, in Delhi and worldwide, than the exhibition itself might have, had it been allowed to proceed undisturbed. I thank heavy-handed officials for giving a well-deserved boost to the photographic talents and career of Raihan Vadra," Tharoor said.The row began after Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, alleged that Bikaner House management had asked him to remove several photographs from his exhibition shortly before its scheduled opening. According to him, the images included photographs documenting student protests and two pictures of the Indian national flag.The Bikaner House Management Society said certain photographs did not comply with its policy and that their removal had been requested. It maintained that photographs meeting the venue's guidelines continued to be displayed.The incident sparked a political confrontation, with Congress leaders criticising the decision as an infringement on artistic expression, while the BJP maintained that exhibitions must follow the venue's rules.Amid the controversy, Keralam chief minister VD Satheesan offered to host the exhibition in its entirety, saying the state would be proud to welcome “No Idea Is Final”, with "no exclusions, no exceptions".However, Kerala BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar questioned the offer, alleging preferential treatment for Raihan Vadra and asking whether ordinary young people received similar attention to their rights and work.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor criticises removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition. He says the move damaged India's global reputation as a freedom-loving democracy. He argues that photographs documenting protest demonstrations depicted events and did not necessarily convey political positions. The Bikaner House Management Society said certain photographs did not comply with its policy.

Article Title: Sudan’s RSF fighters deliberately targeted atleast 43 hospitals during el-Fasher siege: Report
Article Text:
A recent BBC investigation has uncovered alarming evidence of the RSF's assault on numerous healthcare facilities in el-Fasher, Sudan.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A BBC investigation has uncovered evidence suggesting that Sudan’s paramilitary rapid support forces (RSF) systematically targeted and dismantled healthcare facilities in el-Fasher during a prolonged siege and the subsequent capture of the Darfur city a year ago.UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk described the findings as “deeply disturbing”. He said repeated RSF attacks on civilian infrastructure, including medical facilities, constituted serious violations of international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.The RSF has rejected the allegations. The group’s health minister dismissed the findings as propaganda, alleging that Sudan’s national army and its allies were attempting to damage the paramilitary force’s reputation.Drawing on accounts from people who were present in el-fasher, the BBC identified details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and other healthcare facilities between May 2024 and October 2025. Some sites were reportedly struck multiple times.International law prohibits attacks on medical facilities and healthcare workers during armed conflicts.Medical workers killed, injured or abductedThe investigation also documents the impact of the conflict on medical personnel in the western Sudanese city.According to the BBC’s data, 120 healthcare workers were injured, 55 were killed and 10 were forcibly disappeared or abducted between April 2023 and October 2025.Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who worked in el-fasher during the siege, told the BBC that the RSF sought to force hospitals out of operation.“The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state,” he said.Suliman alleged that attacks were intended to make it impossible for civilians to remain in the affected areas, describing the campaign as intense, deliberate and planned.El-Fasher siege marked a brutal phase of Sudan’s warThe investigation was published a year after the fall of el-fasher, one of the most devastating episodes in Sudan’s civil war, which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and the country’s military.Both sides have faced accusations of attacking healthcare facilities.In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned a bombing at al-Daein hospital in eastern Darfur, an area controlled by the RSF. The attack killed dozens of people and forced the facility to close. Sudan’s military was believed to have carried out the drone strikes, but it denied responsibility.Responding to a BBC inquiry, the WHO described the events in el-fasher as “one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan”.UN investigators have also said the violence in el-fasher bore the “hallmarks of genocide”. The city’s population includes non-Arab communities that have faced attacks amid longstanding ethnic tensions, with Arab militias now forming the backbone of the RSF.The BBC investigation provides a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare facilities during the prolonged siege, shedding further light on the conflict’s impact on medical services and civilians.
Article Summary: UN high commissioner for human rights described the findings as 'deeply disturbing' At least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and other healthcare facilities between May 2024 and October 2025. 120 healthcare workers were injured, 55 were killed and 10 were forcibly disappeared or abducted.

NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan at the United Nations, questioning Islamabad's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities while pointing out its failure to safeguard vulnerable communities at home despite criticising New Delhi.Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief on funeral rights in exceptional circumstances on Thursday, India's first secretary to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said, "In Pakistan, the number of minorities is shrinking, and their rights are regularly abused. A state that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India. "She also said human suffering should not be used to serve political interests and called for a more impartial approach to reporting violations of religious freedom.The remarks come against the backdrop of concerns over alleged forced conversions, abductions and marriages involving minority girls in Pakistan, particularly in Sindh.Separately, experts cited by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned that coercion and weak legal safeguards were enabling forced conversions through marriage, particularly among Hindu and Christian communities.The experts emphasised that conversion must be voluntary and that child marriage undermines consent under international law.The Indian representative also questioned the report's emphasis on the funeral rights of terrorists, arguing that the suffering of victims and their families should not be overlooked.She then invoked the 1999 Kargil conflict to challenge Pakistan's position on burials and religious rights, saying Islamabad had refused to accept the bodies of some of its soldiers killed in combat.“It is deeply ironic that a state that did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers who were killed in combat in 1999 in Kargil, unabashedly speaks with fervour on faith, religious freedom and burials,” Mangalanandan said.She added that the Indian Army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic customs.“Let me remind them, it was the Indian Army that buried a number of Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rites,” she said.Mangalanandan also hit out at Pakistan over its comments on Jammu and Kashmir, urging it to turn its attention to areas under its own occupation.“Pakistan's deep obsession with what is happening in the Indian Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir should be actually directed at the developments that are underway in the parts of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, such as Rawalakot,” she said.
Article Summary: India's first secretary to the UN questioned Pakistan's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities. She questioned the report's approach to religious discrimination during the COVID-19 pandemic and its advocacy for the funeral rights of terrorists. Bhavika Mangalanandan also hit out at Pakistan over its comments on Jammu and Kashmir.
