Article Title: Watch: Two Philippine air force trainer aircraft collide mid-air; 4 pilots killed
Article Text:
Crash prompted a temporary grounding of the Air Force’s SF-260 fleet

Four pilots were killed after two Philippine air force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, the military said on Saturday. A video of the incident showed that the planes collided mid-air.The accident occurred on Friday at Fernando Air Base in Batangas province and involved two SF-260 aircraft, the Philippine Air Force said in a statement.Both aircraft crashed within the grounds of the air base. No other casualties were reported, news agency Reuters reported.The air force has temporarily grounded its fleet of SF-260 trainer aircraft pending an investigation into the cause of the crash.The incident follows another fatal crash involving the same aircraft type in May, when two pilots were killed after an SF-260 went down in a mountainous area in the northern Philippines. In 2023, another SF-260 TP Marchetti crashed during a training flight, killing two pilots.
Article Summary: Four pilots killed after two Philippine air force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight. Crash prompted a temporary grounding of the Air Force’s SF-260 fleet. No other casualties were reported, news agency Reuters reported. The incident follows another fatal crash involving the same aircraft type in May.

Article Title: How Jeffrey Epstein became Houthis' new weapon against Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Houthis weaponise Epstein files to target Saudi Arabia's leadership

The Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen is using revelations from the Jeffrey Epstein files to mount a propaganda campaign against Saudi Arabia , seeking to undermine the kingdom's leadership amid renewed fighting between the two sides.The group has seized on reports that associates of the Saudi royal court sent tapestries that once covered the Kaaba, Islam's holiest site in Mecca, to Epstein's private island in the Caribbean. The Houthis have used the allegations to challenge Saudi Arabia's claim to defend Islam.“Those who gave Epstein the Kaaba’s cover are the ones targeting Mecca,” the New York Times quoted Houthi president Mahdi al-Mashat as saying.The remarks followed Saudi Arabia's accusation last month that the Houthis had fired a drone at Mecca in an attempt to provoke Muslims. The militia denied the charge and countered with the allegations involving Epstein.Epstein has also featured in speeches by Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, who has used the case to attack the United States and Israel. “Epstein’s files demand serious attention,” he said in a February address.“They unveil a Zionist incubator that trains leaders and elites.”The messaging comes as Yemen's conflict has intensified again. Saudi Arabia has backed the internationally recognised Yemeni government against the Houthis, whose attacks have targeted Saudi aviation and energy infrastructure. The Saudi-led military intervention in Yemen, which began in 2015, contributed to a devastating humanitarian crisis.The Houthis have also drawn on grievances over the Saudi-led bombing campaign and civilian suffering in Yemen to portray the kingdom as an adversary of Muslims.
Article Summary: Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen is using revelations from the Jeffrey Epstein files to mount a propaganda campaign against Saudi Arabia. The group has seized on reports that associates of the Saudi royal court sent tapestries that once covered the Kaaba to Epstein's private island. The Houthis have used the allegations to challenge Saudi Arabia's claim to defend Islam.

Article Title: ‘838’ number plate, pool of blood, screams: Chilling video captures daylight murder in Maharashtra’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
A video of the incident shows the sequence of events(Credit: X)

:

How the chase ended in murder

Accused surrenders at Cidco police station

Friendship with victim allegedly turned into rivalry

Poll Vote & Share your view Should individuals with a history of violence be monitored more closely? Yes, absolutely No, it's an invasion of privacy 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGARA fancy “838” number plate, a daylight murder and screams of bystanders — horrific scenes unfolded on a busy road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Thursday.A video of the incident shows the sequence of events as a man allegedly runs over his friend with a car before repeatedly bludgeoning him with a stick and an iron rod in broad daylight.The victim, Devesh alias Bunty Dixit (36), died on the spot, while the accused, Pawan Parashar (22), later drove to the Cidco police station and surrendered.Preliminary investigation revealed that Dixit was returning home after a gym session when Parashar, a resident of Wankhedenagar, allegedly began pursuing him in a car.The chase ended near Mangesh Gas Agency in the N-7 area of Cidco. Police said Parashar rammed Dixit’s two-wheeler from behind, throwing him onto the road. The impact was so forceful that the two-wheeler was flung nearly 150 feet away.According to eyewitness accounts cited by police, Parashar then took a U-turn and drove back towards the injured man. He got out of the car and repeatedly struck Dixit on the head with a stick and an iron rod he had carried with him.“After the collision, the accused took a U-turn, drove back to the injured man, got out of the car and repeatedly attacked him on the head with a stick and an iron rod,” said Cidco inspector Atul Yerme.Dixit succumbed to his injuries at the spot before medical assistance could reach him.The killing triggered panic in the locality, with passersby and shopkeepers gathering at the scene. Senior police officers, including deputy commissioner of police (Zone II) Ratnakar Navale, visited the spot.Parashar subsequently drove to the Cidco police station and surrendered, police said.Police suspect that a fallout between the two men led to the killing.“The accused, after surrendering before the police, claimed that he and the victim used to work as bouncers for different bars. He was upset due to their friendship turning into a rivalry,” Navale told TOI.He said police teams were cross-verifying the accused’s version and probing the exact motive behind the murder.Inspector (Crime) Gajanan Kalyankar said investigators were questioning Parashar to establish the complete sequence of events and ascertain the circumstances that led to the killing.
Article Summary: Devesh alias Bunty Dixit (36) died on the spot, while the accused, Pawan Parashar (22), later drove to the Cidco police station and surrendered. Police suspect that a fallout between the two men led to the killing. The accused claimed that he and the victim used to work as bouncers for different bars.

Article Title: Woman medical officer assaulted, slapped and abused in police presence; video viral
Article Text:
CCTV footage of the incident, which occurred around midnight on Wednesday, went viral on social media.





WARDHA: A woman medical officer was allegedly assaulted and verbally abused by an accused brought by police for a medical examination at the primary health centre (PHC) in Talegaon Shyamji Pant, Ashti taluka of Wardha district.The accused was allegedly under the influence of alcohol when he charged at the doctor.CCTV footage of the incident, which occurred around midnight on Wednesday, went viral on social media. Medical officers across the district boycotted work in protest on Thursday.The accused, Kadir Ali Razzaq Ali, a resident of Talegaon, was accompanied by two police personnel and three home guards when he allegedly slapped the woman medical officer and used obscene language, sources said. Even after being taken out of the outpatient department (OPD), he allegedly continued to abuse her.Six months ago, a patient’s relative had assaulted a doctor at the same PHC. Angered by the latest attack, healthcare staff marched to Talegaon police station to protest. Based on the medical officer’s complaint, police registered a case against Kadir Ali on Thursday.The incident has raised questions about security arrangements for medical personnel during examinations of accused persons brought in by police.Alleged illegal sale of alcohol, ganja and gutka in the area has also drawn attention.Dilip Utane of AITUC and the Maharashtra State Medical Officers’ Federation condemned the assault. Medical officers also submitted a memorandum of demands to district collector Vanmathi C., chief executive officer Parag Soman and superintendent of police Saurabhkumar Agrawal.The Federation demanded strict action against the accused, along with administrative action against the police personnel who allegedly failed to take adequate precautions while bringing him for examination. It also called for special measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.The Federation also announced that accused persons would no longer undergo medical examinations at PHCs.
Article Summary: CCTV footage of the incident, which occurred around midnight on Wednesday, went viral on social media. Medical officers across the district boycotted work in protest on Thursday. Kadir Ali Razzaq Ali, a resident of Talegaon, was accompanied by two police personnel and three home guards.

Article Title: 'Now is the time': Rubio warns Cuba next after Iran, asks Cubans to join hands with CIA
Article Text:
Rubio accused the Cuban government officials of living corrupt and privileged lives while disappointing citizens with failed promises (Photo: ANI).

Trump hints Cuba next after Iran

US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Friday called upon Cubans to "discreetly" join hands with the US intelligence agencies in order to bring about a "positive change" in Cuba, removing the communist regime."To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio said in a post on X.Rubio accused the Cuban government officials of living corrupt and privileged lives while disappointing citizens with failed promises."The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA ," he said.Hours later, the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) posted a video on X in Spanish, Cuba's official language, outlining how people with information of interest to the agency could contact it. The agency advised them to visit an official US facility in person as their first option, provided they could travel there safely.For those seeking to contact the CIA online through its official website, the agency recommended using a secure internet connection, such as a VPN, along with a private browser and a burner email account not linked to personal details.The agency also advised those submitting information to include their city, occupation, level of access and contact details in their message.The CIA’s recruitment appeal drew mockery from Cuban officials.“Now the United States is resorting to public recruitment for the CIA,” Cuban Deputy Foreign Minister Carlos Fernandez de Cossio wrote on X.“There must be a great deal of desperation or misery within the agency for it to be forced to sell its services like a tube of toothpaste,” he added.On Friday, US President Donald Trump mentioned he sought a regime change in Cuba as he spoke during a rally in Florida.Trump said that US warships returning from the Middle East could then militarily engage with Cuba.“We’ll do a little stopover,” Trump said.“Actually, what we’re going to do with Cuba is, we’re going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.”Trump's remarks drew sharp criticism from Cuba, with Cuban foreign minister Bruno Rodriguez dismissing Trump's threats."Our coastline is full of beautiful beaches, but there are also razor-sharp limestone spikes, an inhospitable environment for those who make it to our shores with hostile purposes and lust for domination," Rodriguez said in an X post.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Friday called upon Cubans to "discreetly" join hands with the US intelligence agencies. Rubio accused the Cuban government officials of living corrupt and privileged lives while disappointing citizens with failed promises. Hours later, the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) posted a video on X in Spanish, Cuba's official language, outlining how people with information of interest to the agency could contact it.

Article Title: Watch: Iran mocks Trump on busy Tehran street, shows US president taking nap behind bars
Article Text:
A Trump impersonator rattles the bars of a mock jail cell and takes a nap inside a Tehran billboard targeting the US over a deadly strike on an Iranian wedding

A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran, where he can be seen rattling the bars and taking a nap in a staged display targeting Washington over a deadly strike on an Iranian wedding.The installation, placed above Tajrish Square, one of Tehran's busiest transport hubs, features an actor wearing a Trump mask and wig inside a mock prison cell equipped with a bed, toilet and sink. The performance has drawn crowds, with passersby stopping to film the spectacle.An electronic billboard behind the cage displays images related to a US strike that hit a wedding in the southern Iranian town of Kuhestak last month. The display also features crime-scene imagery, linking the attack to its message against the US president.The installation was unveiled on Tuesday by Tehran's Beautification Organization, which is affiliated with the city's municipality, according to Iranian state media. It appears to be part of a 15-day campaign highlighting the wedding strike.The display comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.Also Read: 'Another little Epic Fury': Trump issues new warning; Iran says 'don't play with fire' Tehran has increasingly used public billboards to deliver political messages against Washington, including a previous display showing Trump lying in a graffiti-covered coffin.Iranian authorities and supporters have also circulated online memes and videos mocking Trump and his administration during the conflict.The wedding strike has become a focus of the latest campaign. US Central Command had said it was aware of Iranian reports about the incident and that American forces do not target civilians.
Article Summary: A life-sized impersonator of US President Donald Trump has been put inside a jail-like cage mounted on a billboard in Tehran. The performance has drawn crowds, with passersby stopping to film the spectacle. The display comes amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.

Article Title: Thousands bang utensils in ‘noise protest’ across Manipur valley districts
Article Text:
People bang utensils during a protest in Imphal Friday

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the recent noise protests in Manipur? Yes, absolutely No, I do not 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GUWAHATI: Thousands of people across Manipur ’s five valley districts took to the streets on Friday evening for a “noise protest” invoking traditional Kangla practices to express public anger over the ongoing crisis in the state and against govt’s failure to restore normalcy.Police fired tear gas shells at Kangla Fort in Imphal as tensions mounted. No injuries were reported.The protest was called by a civil society organisation, Federation of Haomee, which asked people to make noise between 7:30 pm and 8 pm.Residents banged utensils, struck electric poles with hammers, beat drums, sounded vehicle horns and sirens and shouted slogans.The protest was also at Singjamei, the assembly constituency of chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, where residents joined the demonstration against govt’s handling of the prolonged ethnic conflict.Many protesters then marched towards Kangla, the ancient political and cultural centre of the erstwhile Manipur kingdom, a few metres from Lok Bhavan and the chief minister’s secretariat.Security forces stopped several of them at Palace Compound, Moirangkhom and Keisampat junctions. Hundreds more reached the gate of Kangla but were not allowed into the fort premises.The protesters demanded the implementation of National Register of Citizens (NRC) in the state, the identification of illegal immigrants and the abrogation of Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with armed groups. They also criticised govt’s failure to resolve the ethnic conflict.The demonstrations reflected growing public frustration over continued violence and demands for decisive action on security following days of sit-ins and rallies over the killing of three Meitei woodcutters at Sunurok on Oct 19.
Article Summary: Police fired tear gas shells at Kangla Fort in Imphal as tensions mounted. Protesters banged utensils, struck electric poles with hammers, beat drums, sounded vehicle horns and sirens and shouted slogans. Protesters demanded implementation of National Register of Citizens (NRC) in the state.

Article Title: Sting operation bid to blackmail me, tarnish image: Siddaramaiah
Article Text:
Karnataka ex CM Siddaramaiah

Don't need anyone's support: Ex-CM





MYSURU/BENGALURU: Breaking his silence on the viral sting video, former CM Siddaramaiah Friday claimed it was meant to "blackmail" him and "tarnish" his image, while his son and urban development minister Yathindra blamed members of the Congress for the sting op.Within hours, KPCC president BK Hariprasad ordered show-cause notices to party workers seen in the video, which was first flagged by Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, leaving CM DK Shivakumar in a tight spot.The former CM said he had filed a police complaint and sought a court injunction against telecasting of the video because he wanted to know who was behind it."Only an investigation will reveal that. There is no need for an SIT as I have full faith in the ongoing police probe," he added.No such case was foisted on him in his eight years as CM or since he became a minister in 1984, Siddaramaiah said. The video surfaced only after he exited office, he noted, wondering how anyone could pressure him when he was out of power. Asked if he was disappointed, he said it's a concocted story.He named former child welfare committee chairperson Kripa Alva and Power TV MD Rakesh Shetty as those seen in the video and dismissed their allegations as baseless.On Kumaraswamy's moral support, he said: "I don't need anyone's support. I want people to know the truth."Yathindra said people from his own party wanted to "destroy my father's legacy". Kumaraswamy had alleged Shivakumar was behind the sting operations.Pointing to the viral video, Yathindra said: "As she herself says in the video, she wanted a ticket from Puttur. Prima facie, the sting appears to have been conducted for that purpose. Just because a worker has done something like this, it does not mean our party is against us. Probe must establish whether those involved acted on their own or someone was pulling the strings. As of now, we do not suspect anyone."Hariprasad said action will follow once replies to the notices come in and if evidence shows Congress members are involved.
Article Summary: Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah breaks his silence on the viral sting video. He claims it was meant to "blackmail" him and "tarnish" his image. His son and urban development minister Yathindra blamed members of the Congress for the sting op.

Article Title: Class 11 student murder case: Accused opens fire at Chandigarh police during weapon recovery, shot in leg
Article Text:
During a recent police operation, Manmehar Preet Singh reportedly fired at officers, hitting ASI Pradeep's bulletproof vest while they were recovering a weapon tied to Naitik Khandelwal's murder in Sector 22

Accused allegedly snatched pistol and opened fire

Father works in

Punjab Police

intelligence wing





CHANDIGARH: In a dramatic development in the murder of Naitik Khandelwal in Sector 22, accused shooter Manmehar Preet Singh alias Mann, of Kharar, allegedly opened fire at a police team during a weapon recovery operation in the Sector 50 forest area early on Saturday. A bullet hit ASI Pradeep’s bulletproof jacket, saving him from serious injury. Police retaliated, hitting Manmehar in his right leg.The injured accused was taken to Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Sector 32, for treatment. His brother, Arsh, was also present at the spot during the operation.According to police, the Operation Cell team, under the supervision of Inspector Harinder Singh Shekhon, had taken the two brothers, Mann and Arsh, to the forest area to recover the weapon allegedly used in Naitik’s murder. During the investigation, the accused had reportedly disclosed that the weapon had been concealed in the forest area.Police said that during the recovery operation, Manmehar allegedly pushed a police personnel and attempted to escape from custody. He then snatched a pistol and fired at the police team, with the bullet striking ASI Pradeep’s bulletproof jacket.The police personnel retaliated, and a bullet hit Manmehar in his right leg. He was subsequently taken to GMCH-32 for treatment.The police are carrying out further investigations into the incident and the weapon recovery. The circumstances surrounding the firing are also being examined.Manmehar and Arsh’s father is reportedly posted in the intelligence wing of the Punjab Police. Investigators are probing the alleged roles of Manmehar and Arsh in Naitik’s murder.Police are also investigating the source of the weapon allegedly used in the killing and whether any other person was involved in the crime.
Article Summary: Accused shooter Manmehar Preet Singh, of Kharar, allegedly opened fire at a police team during a weapon recovery operation in the Sector 50 forest area. A bullet hit ASI Pradeep’s bulletproof jacket, saving him from serious injury. The injured accused was taken to Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, for treatment.

Article Title: 'Cyclone Arnab': IMD warns Bay of Bengal system may intensify; Andhra-Odisha coast on alert
Article Text:
Forecasts indicate a low-pressure system emerging over the Bay of Bengal, which could potentially transform into a cyclonic storm





KOLKATA: A low-pressure area brewing over Bay of Bengal is set to strengthen into the year’s first tropical cyclonic storm, which could hit the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast on the night of Oct 28 (Wednesday). The Met office said in its initial forecast that the system may trigger showers in Bengal, including light to moderate rain in Kolkata from Tuesday and a few heavy spells in the coastal belt on Wednesday and Thursday.If the system intensifies into a cyclone, it would be called Arnab (meaning ocean), a name given by Bangladesh.The low-pressure area and an associated cyclonic circulation extending up to 5.8 km above the mean sea level formed over east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday morning, according to a special IMD bulletin. The composite system is likely to persist over the same region and intensify into a depression on Oct 24.“Thereafter, it is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression on Oct 25 and into a cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Oct 26 morning. It would then continue to intensify further and move west-northwestwards towards North Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts during the subsequent two days,” according to a special bulletin issued by IMD.The Met office said that while it was too early to predict the trajectory of the system, the coastal Bengal will start feeling its impact from Tuesday in the form of squally winds.“Heavy rainfall activity very likely to occur at one or two places over some districts of West Bengal during Oct 28 to 30,” said the bulletin.H R Biswas, of Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata, said the city is likely to receive light to moderate rain from Tuesday. “If the system intensifies into a cyclone, this will be the first cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal this year. While Bengal is unlikely to fall in the direct trajectory of the system, coastal Bengal is likely to receive a few spells of heavy rain. We have issued a warning for fishermen,” said Biswas.The period from Oct to Dec is conducive to the formation of cyclones over Bay of Bengal.“We are continuously monitoring the system, which might intensify further after transforming into a cyclonic storm. But it is too early to say how far it will intensify,” Biswas said.A cyclonic storm can intensify further into a severe, a very severe, an extremely severe or a super cyclone.
Article Summary: A low-pressure area brewing over Bay of Bengal is set to strengthen into the year’s first tropical cyclonic storm. The system could hit the Andhra Pradesh- Odisha coast on the night of Oct 28 (Wednesday) The Met office said in its initial forecast that the system may trigger showers in Bengal.

Article Title: Delhi HC junks Neha Bora plea against peace bond notice
Article Text:
The Delhi high court has denied AISA president Neha Bora's request to challenge a peace bond notice

‘Orders breached under BNSS Section 163 despite warning’





NEW DELHI: There was "sufficient material" before the special executive magistrate to proceed against AISA president Neha Bora over apprehensions of breach of peace and disturbance of public tranquillity, Delhi high court said Friday. It dismissed her plea challenging a notice asking her to execute a peace bond, a day before she has to appear before the official.The notice was issued under BNSS Section 126, which empowers the SEM to enforce the signing of a bond if there is credible information that a person is likely to breach peace, disturb public tranquillity, or commit a wrongful act that may cause disturbance.Justice Subramonium Prasad said the “area where the petitioner was detained and where she was urging people to join her protest is a commercial area, receiving very high footfall from office-goers, and there are important roads connecting the heart of the city to various other areas. There are a large number of hotels, banks, offices, vendors and, therefore, it cannot be said that there was no material at all before the SEM before proceeding against the petitioner. ”HC said the SEM’s notice “further gets fortified when prohibitory orders under Section 163 of BNSS had been passed covering the said area, i.e., Mandi House”.Noting that Bora has been named in six FIRs by Delhi Police, the court said “even one incident is sufficient” to initiate proceedings under Chapter IX of BNSS (provisions related to security for keeping the peace and for good behaviour) if the “circumstances so suggest that there is an apprehension that such a person will indulge in further incidents of the same nature which can breach peace and disturb public tranquillity”.HC said in the case before it, “it has been recorded that the petitioner has breached the orders under Section 163 of BNSS despite being warned” while finding merit in the SEM’s show-cause notice.Challenging the police notice, Bora’s lawyer had argu-ed that there was no application of mind or independent opinion at the time of issuance of the notice.
Article Summary: Delhi high court denies AISA president Neha Bora's request to challenge a peace bond notice. Court says there was "sufficient material" before the special executive magistrate to proceed against Bora. Bora has been named in six FIRs by Delhi Police.

Article Title: Dehradun school teacher sacked after student alleges molestation
Article Text:
(Representative) A private school has expelled a physics teacher amidst allegations of harassment made by a student





DEHRADUN: A private school in Dehradun has terminated a physics teacher following allegations of repeated harassment and molestation by a Class 11 student, though police are yet to receive a formal complaint in the matter.The incident came to light earlier this month when the student’s family lodged a complaint with the school on Oct 15, alleging that the teacher had harassed and molested the girl several times in the preceding weeks.The principal said the school’s internal committee began an inquiry as soon as the complaint was received, and the teacher was immediately asked to leave the premises. “Even though there wasn’t any conclusive evidence, we took the complaint seriously and terminated the teacher the very next day,” the principal said, adding that the student was assured of all possible assistance.On Friday, the family returned to the school, alleging that the matter had not been handled properly and demanding stricter action. They also claimed that other students had faced similar issues which the school neglected. Police were called to defuse the situation.“We did take action immediately,” the principal said.SP (city) Shekhar Suyal said no formal police complaint had been filed so far. “As soon as they approach us, we will do the needful,” he said.
Article Summary: A private school in Dehradun has terminated a physics teacher following allegations of repeated harassment and molestation by a Class 11 student. The incident came to light earlier this month when the student’s family lodged a complaint with the school. Police are yet to receive a formal complaint in the matter.

Article Title: Husband’s illicit relationship by itself is not cruelty: Madras high court
Article Text:
Madras high court ruled that a husband's illicit relationship is not sufficient for cruelty under Section 498A.





CHENNAI: A husband’s illicit relationship with another woman by itself would not amount to cruelty to a married woman – a criminal offence under Section 498A of the IPC -- Madras high court has observed.“It is well settled that to attract the offence under Section 498A of IPC, something more than a mere illicit relationship has to be established by the prosecution,” Justice Sunder Mohan said on Friday. This position is reiterated by the Supreme Court judgment in the case of Pinakin Mahipatray Rawal Vs State of Gujarat, he added.The court made the observations while dismissing an appeal moved by brother of a deceased woman, who committed suicide along with her one-and-a-half-year-old child, allegedly due to her husband’s illicit relationship and dowry harassment.On April 23, 2018, a Mahila court acquitted the husband from all the charges on the ground that the prosecution had not established the dowry demand and also the illicit relationship of the husband and that there was no evidence to suggest cruelty of such nature which will drive a woman to commit suicide.Since the state failed to prefer an appeal against the acquittal, the deceased woman’s brother who was the defacto complainant moved the high court.“The reason for acquittal by the trial judge that the illicit relationship had not been established because the lady with whom the husband had an illicit relationship was not examined is perverse. However, the fact that the husband had an illicit relationship by itself would not amount to cruelty in terms of Section 498A of IPC,” the court said.Hence, on an independent assessment of the evidence, this court finds that the prosecution had not established its case, though the reasons for acquittal by the trial court cannot be accepted, the judge said and dismissed the appeal.
Article Summary: Madras high court ruled that a husband's illicit relationship is not sufficient for cruelty under Section 498A. The court made the observations while dismissing an appeal moved by brother of a deceased woman, who committed suicide along with her one-and-a-half-year-old child.

Article Title: Urad dal, roti and 6am wake-up call: Influencer-model Shraddha Dubey adjusts to life inside Lucknow jail
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey and her sister Rashmi have transitioned to a general women’s barrack at the Gosai Ganj District Jail

How police traced the accused to Nagpur





LUCKNOW: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the murder of Lucknow restaurateur Shiva Sharma, and her sister Rashmi Dubey have been moved to the general women's barrack at Gosai Ganj District Jail after completing their quarantine period. The sisters, who were reportedly used to a lavish lifestyle, are now adjusting to the prison's strict routine and regular meals.The two were lodged in jail on Thursday and shifted to a barrack housing 45 female inmates on Friday. According to the jail administration, Shraddha appeared tense when she arrived on Thursday night and could not finish her first meal, which included whole urad dal, roti and potato-soy fenugreek curry.The sisters reportedly had a restless night and were woken up at 6am on Friday as per jail rules. They were served sweet porridge and tea for breakfast, followed by whole urad dal, rajma, potato-bottle gourd curry, rice and roti for lunch. Dinner comprised arhar dal, potato-pumpkin curry and roti. Jail officials said the sisters were receiving the same food as other inmates.Neither sister received a visit from relatives on Friday. They reportedly remained quiet in the barrack throughout the day and did not interact with other inmates, although they were occasionally seen talking to each other.Jail officials said they were gradually getting used to the prison environment.District Jail Jailer Ritwik Priyadarshi said Shraddha, Rashmi and their driver, Tanveer alias Danish, had been moved to regular barracks after completing quarantine. A female deputy jailer is monitoring the sisters, while a male deputy jailer is supervising Tanveer. For security reasons, all three will appear before the court through video conferencing on their scheduled judicial custody dates.Meanwhile, investigators are looking into the alleged role of people who may have helped the accused after Sharma's death. Police found that Rashmi had allegedly called a man named Aamir for help shortly after Sharma fell from the building. CCTV footage obtained from the hospital reportedly shows Aamir Sheikh, wearing a black T-shirt, with Tanveer alias Danish. Police teams are now searching for those suspected of helping the accused.Shraddha, Rashmi and Danish were arrested in Nagpur on October 20 after Lucknow Police tracked their movements through WhatsApp calls, internet connection details and information provided by a cab driver.Investigators said the trio had repeatedly changed locations to evade arrest. The frequent moves made it difficult for police to catch up with them, as internet connection details used for surveillance took around 14 to 15 hours to reach investigators, leaving the teams nearly three hours behind the suspects.Police said the accused allegedly stayed at each location for less than 12 hours before moving elsewhere to avoid detection. The investigation gained momentum after officers traced and questioned a cab driver who had taken the trio to Nagpur.According to investigators, Shraddha mainly used her driver Danish's mobile phone for WhatsApp calls. During the journey, she allegedly accessed the internet through a hotspot provided by the cab driver.The driver dropped the trio in Nagpur late on October 19 and waited outside a hotel for another passenger travelling to Kanpur. Police traced him and questioned him, and the information he provided helped narrow the search.A Lucknow Police team then reached Nagpur and increased surveillance, waiting for another WhatsApp call that could reveal the suspects' location. Shraddha allegedly made a call that helped investigators trace the signal to a flat in the Pro-Zone Calm apartment complex in Chinchbhan.When officers reached the flat on the afternoon of October 20, the occupants allegedly refused to open the door. Police sought assistance from Nagpur Police, after which the door was opened and the three were arrested.They were subsequently brought back to Lucknow. Police had announced a reward of Rs 50,000 each for information leading to their arrest.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment near Balu Adda in Lucknow's Hazratganj area. His death triggered the investigation that led to the arrest of Shraddha and her associates.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey and her sister Rashmi have transitioned to a general women’s barrack at the Gosai Ganj District Jail. The sisters, who were used to a lavish lifestyle, are now adjusting to the prison's strict routine and regular meals.

Article Title: 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members condemn ‘unprecedented’ police action against protesting students, seek explanation from institute director
Article Text:
Twenty-one IIT-Bombay faculty members wrote to the director condemning police actions against protesting students.





MUMBAI: As many as 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members have written to the institute’s director, condemning what they called ‘unprecedented’ police action against students peacefully protesting on campus on Sunday and seeking an explanation.A small section of students have been protesting for over a month after second-year B Tech student Sahil Wakode died by suicide on Sept 18. They have been demanding action and accountability from the institute since then.The letter, sent on Monday, came a day after students were twice detained from the campus protest site, dubbed as ‘Justice Corner’. Police also allegedly dismantled the protest site, removing banners and posters. Sahil’s parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, who visited the institute to pay homage to him alleged they were forcibly taken to Azad Maidan police station and detained till 6pm.The faculty members, in the letter, sought to know whether any institute functionary had authorised police action. If not, they asked whether the administration would seek an FIR against the police officers responsible for the “act of violence” committed against the students.At the outset, the faculty members acknowledged differing views on the ongoing protest, with some considering it irrelevant or damaging to IIT-B’s reputation, while others viewed it as a necessary call for the institute to reflect on its educational commitments and responsibilities amid its history of student suicides. They condemned the forceful removal of students who have been peacefully protesting for several weeks.The faculty members sought explanations from the administration regarding who authorised police to enter the campus and detain students, the use of ‘brute force’ during both rounds of detention, and the alleged failure of institute officials to intervene or help the detainees. “We have learnt that students detained at the police station tried to contact the dean of student affairs, Quick Response Team and chief security officer for help, but their requests were not entertained and that no institute functionary came to the police station. What accounts for it?” they asked.They also questioned the alleged vandalism at the protest site, which displayed images of Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, and Dr B R Ambedkar. They sought an explanation for the administration’s refusal to return students’ personal belongings, including laptops, and asked whether due procedure had been followed in seizing them.IIT-B authorities did not comment on the letter.Sources claimed that police had come to the campus only because Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad planned to visit that day. The institute had not responded to the MP’s letter seeking permission, and her visit coincided with a visit by Wakode’s parents.Sources also claimed that students jeering at police minutes before Gaikwad and Wakode’s parents arrived had prompted the detentions. Regarding the confiscation of personal belongings, they claimed that the items were lying at the gate and blocking the entrance. The institute plans to return them to the students in accordance with its lost-and-found SOP, they added.
Article Summary: 21 IIT-Bombay faculty members have written to the institute’s director condemning what they called ‘unprecedented’ police action. A small section of students have been protesting for over a month after second-year B Tech student Sahil Wakode died by suicide on Sept 18. They have been demanding action and accountability from the institute.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing: Rs 2 lakh paid to shooters, logistics team, cops trace UPI transfers; 2 factory-made firearms not recovered yet
Article Text:
Three individuals were arrested in connection to the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff and brought to Mumbai.





MUMBAI: The three persons allegedly involved in the firing at actor Tiger Shroff were brought back to Mumbai from Kota on Wednesday morning and remanded in police custody till Oct 31.Preliminary ballistic reports have suggested the shooters while firing at actor Tiger Shroff used two factory-made firearms which are yet to be recovered. The three accused shooters-Phool Singh (18), Rehan Ansari (18), and Rithik Kumar alias Roshan (22)-who were arrested from Kota were produced before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court which remanded them to police custody till Oct 31.Cops, while seeking police custody of the accused, told the court that the accused have destroyed the mobile phones used in connection with the crime, making the reconstruction of their communications through social media apps a key part of the investigation.Police are attempting to establish contact between the shooters and their alleged handlers, including Shubham Lonkar, through other digital evidence and their interrogation.The shooters had arrived in Mumbai on Sept 20, police said. "So far, investigation suggests the shooters and those who provided logistic support received around Rs 2 lakh, with which they bought a second-hand bike for Rs 25,000. Another Rs 37,000 was transferred in the account of Rehan Ansari.There were some more cash payments which are being ascertained," said Raj Tilak Roshan, deputy commissioner of police. Investigators are also examining the payments made through UPI applications and cash.Ansari and Singh's lawyer, Ajinkya Mirgal, argued that the police have already interrogated them in two days' transit remand and they should be sent to judicial custody.According to the preliminary investigation, Anil Pandit allegedly contacted Sameer, who also allegedly contacted Ansari.Ansari is suspected of having brought together Phool Singh and Rithik Kumar, the two accused alleged to have carried out the firing at Shroff.The five others, including two women, who have been arrested allegedly played roles in procuring, transporting and supplying weapons to the shooters and providing logistical support to the group. One of them, Radha, a bar girl, was a friend of accused Kunal. The duo came to Mumbai along with Babita, another accused. While Kunal left Mumbai the same day, the two women stayed in an Andheri lodge, delivered the weapons, and left later. They are being brought to Mumbai and will be produced before a court on Thursday.Sources associated with the probe suggested the accused monitored Shroff's movements through social media posts, videos and reels shared by the actor and his fans. The accused had done a survey of this playground in Juhu for 10 days. The shooters had even laid out a plan on Oct 11 but the actor did not turn up.
Article Summary: Three individuals were arrested in connection to the firing incident involving actor Tiger Shroff and brought to Mumbai. The three accused shooters-Phool Singh (18), Rehan Ansari (18) and Rithik Kumar alias Roshan (22)-who were arrested from Kota were produced before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate Court which remanded them to police custody till Oct 31.

A 37-year-old man, Biru Singh Bhadauriya, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area.

KANPUR: A 37-year-old man died on Wednesday after he was allegedly assaulted, pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped between its window panes and dragged for around 1.5km by a group of attackers in Kanpur’s Hanumant Vihar area.Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation.The incident took place on Tuesday night when Biru Singh Bhadauriya was returning home after visiting a Dussehra fair. The attackers allegedly rammed their car into him over an old rivalry before assaulting him and forcing him onto the vehicle’s roof.They allegedly trapped both his hands between the window panes, shut the windows and drove at high speed for around 1.5km with Bhadauriya on the roof. The attackers then allegedly threw him onto the road and fled.Bhadauriya was rushed to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital, where he died during treatment on Wednesday.According to a post on the official Kanpur Commissionerate police handle, a man was seriously injured after being hit by an unidentified vehicle on Arra Road on Tuesday night. He succumbed to his injuries during treatment at Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital the following day.Police said a case had been registered under relevant sections and the postmortem examination had been conducted. Further legal action is underway, with investigators examining CCTV footage to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved.
Article Summary: Biru Singh Bhadauriya, 37, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area. He was allegedly pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped between its window panes and dragged for around 1.5km by a group of attackers. Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation.

Article Title: Unnao murder mystery: How woman and YouTuber friend killed her husband in room, stuffed his body in box and transported 21km away
Article Text:
(AI IMAGE) Unnao police solved a murder case involving the body of a man found in a box on a highway.





KANPUR: Unnao police have solved the murder of a young man whose body was found locked inside a box on a highway service lane and arrested his 28-year-old wife, Neha Rawat, and YouTuber Jitendra alias Rahul Singh for allegedly killing him.According to police, Neha and Jitendra allegedly killed Sonu Savita (28) at his rented room in Kanchan Nagar, Shuklaganj, on Monday night before transporting the body 21 km to Lalaookheda in the Sadar area.CCTV footage helped police trace the loader used to transport the box. Investigators found that the vehicle’s driver had no role in the crime.Police said Jitendra allegedly consumed alcohol with Sonu from around 9 pm. Around midnight, after Sonu became heavily intoxicated, Neha allegedly struck him on the head with a grinding stone (sil-batta). She and Jitendra then allegedly assaulted him with bamboo sticks and smothered him with a blanket, causing his death.Around 6 pm on Tuesday, Jitendra allegedly paid Rs 10,000 to two labourers, including a minor to help move the box.The accused allegedly hired a loader for Rs 1,200 and misled its driver by claiming they were shifting accommodation.Neha and the two labourers travelled in the vehicle and unloaded the box on the service lane of the Unnao-Lalganj highway around 8 pm. A bulldozer repair shop operator noticed it about an hour later and informed police.Sonu, a resident of Panchamkheda village in Hasanganj, had met Neha nine years ago. Police said she later left her husband, Jagdish, and four daughters and moved in with Sonu in Shuklaganj. After living together for two years, the couple solemnised a court marriage.Investigators said Neha later became close to Jitendra, who had rented a room in the same house.SP Jaiprakash Singh said the preliminary investigation indicated that the deceased’s wife and her YouTuber friend were involved in the murder. Two other individuals have also been detained, and further legal proceedings are under way, he added.
Article Summary: Unnao police have solved the murder of a young man whose body was found locked inside a box on a highway service lane. Police arrested his 28-year-old wife, Neha Rawat, and YouTuber Jitendra alias Rahul Singh for allegedly killing him.

Article Title: 15-year-old girl raped by 3 men after running away from home in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
A distressing event unfolded when a 15-year-old girl fled her home in Tirunelveli after a family dispute (Representative image)





MADURAI: Two men were arrested for raping a 15-year-old girl stranded in Tiruchendur after running away from home. Two minor boys have also been booked under Pocso Act The Class X student had left her home in Tirunelveli on Oct 15 after arguing with her parents over failing an exam, said police. When she did not return, the parents lodged a ‘missing person’ complaint with the Thalaiyuthu police.The girl had boarded a train to Tiruchendur with her boyfriend and another friend. The boys harassed her during the trip, said police. After learning from their parents that police were after them, they handed her some money and abandoned her.At Tiruchendur, three men from Madurai — Karthik Shanmugasundaram and Mani — approached her, offering assistance. They took her to Kulasekarapattinam where a Dasara festival was under way. Mani, 28, raped her before leaving town with Shanmugasundaram.Police said the men had gone to the fest to commit theft.Karthik, 26, a divorcee, promised to marry her and took her to his house in Vadipatti on Oct 16, and raped her, said police. She escaped with help from locals and reached Mattuthavani bus stand in Madurai.Tirunelveli police traced her to Vadipatti, and rescued her from Mattuthavani on Oct 17. Police had used CCTV footage and facial recognition to trace the whereabouts of the girl and the three men.Mani and Shanmugasundaram were remanded in judicial custody on Tuesday. Karthik was remanded by the Dindigul police. Police said the two minors would be produced before Juvenile Justice Board and sent to an observation home.
Article Summary: The Class X student had left her home in Tirunelveli on Oct 15 after arguing with her parents over failing an exam. When she did not return, the parents lodged a ‘missing person’ complaint with the Thalaiyuthu police. Two minor boys have also been booked under Pocso Act.

Article Title: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest U-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik killed in late-night road accident on Cuttack highway
Article Text:
Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malay Barik, two talented athletes from Odisha, tragically lost their lives in an accident





BHUBANESWAR: Two promising Odisha athletes, Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night.Dondapati had emerged as one of the country's fastest sprinters in the under-23 category in 2025, while Barik competed in the 400m event. Their deaths have left Odisha's sporting fraternity mourning the loss of two young athletes.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths in a social media post."Deeply saddened by the tragic demise of athletes Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malaya Barik in a road accident. Their untimely passing is a profound loss to Odisha's sporting fraternity," Majhi said.Offering condolences to the bereaved families, he prayed to Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath to give them strength to cope with the loss and grant eternal peace to the departed souls.
Article Summary: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night. Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths.
